divergence_justification: Human override of the attempt 0002 block; see mimic-iv/concepts_fhir/human_override/nsaid.md for the full argument. Same cause as antibiotic and the same statement: mimic-fhir/sql/fhir_medication_request.sql:172-177 emits MedicationRequest.dispenseRequest.validityPeriod only when 'ph_STARTTIME IS NOT NULL AND ph_STARTTIME <= ph_STOPTIME', dropping both endpoints together, and no other served element carries prescriptions.starttime/stoptime (authoredOn at :55,124 is pharmacy entertime; fhir_medication_dispense.sql carries none; fhir_medication_administration.sql:177 is emar charttime at another grain; identifiers carry identity only and resource-id inversion is refused per LOOP_CONTRACT.md:317-333). This explains all 10,276 differing_null_only rows (starttime NULL 10,276; stoptime NULL 10,249), decomposing into 10,249 reversed intervals that FHIR R4 Period invariant per-1 makes intrinsically unrepresentable and 27 one-sided-NULL-stoptime rows lost to a NULL-unsafe guard, a small fixable upstream defect. The 18 differing_conflict rows (starttime 12, stoptime 6) were replayed in full by the comparator as the exempt TIMESTAMPTZ DST cast at :43-44 (conflict_attribution.complete true) and the judge did not block on them. Not essential loss per LOOP_CONTRACT.md:481: row counts equal at 235,678 with delta 0, the residual paired 1:1 on (subject_id, hadm_id, nsaid) with matching multiplicity and zero only_oracle/only_candidate, nsaid.sql:30-35 is a filtered projection with no GROUP BY, window, carry-forward, derived column or stay_id, every gap is a typed NULL rather than an estimate, and concept_dag finds no consumer of mimiciv_derived.nsaid so nothing inherits the gap. Fidelity 225,384/235,678 identical (95.6317%). Consistency: acei (9,059/112,014 = 8.09%) and arb (3,179/39,534 = 8.04%) are the same query shape over prescriptions with the same gap at larger fractions and were judge-accepted; blocking nsaid at 4.36% turned on which judge invocation saw it, which LOOP_CONTRACT.md:512-516 rules against.

reopen_history.reason: Downstream SQL-on-FHIR consumers join derived tables on getResourceKey() resource keys, which the port computes internally but drops at the outermost SELECT. The attempt adds the paired key column beside each MIMIC identifier column (subject_id->patient_key, hadm_id->encounter_key, stay_id->icu_encounter_key, specimen_id->specimen_key). Additive and shape-only: both comparison paths project manifest columns explicitly, so no compared value can change. The MIMIC integer columns are retained as the oracle join keys.
reopen_history.superseded_justification: Human override of the judge's blocked ruling on the same artifact; no rerun, the comparison is unchanged. The 10,276 differing_null_only rows are MedicationRequest.dispenseRequest.validityPeriod.start/end, which mimic-fhir/sql/fhir_medication_request.sql:172-176 emits only WHEN ph_STARTTIME IS NOT NULL AND (ph_STARTTIME <= ph_STOPTIME) -- so an invalid or reversed prescription interval carries no period at all. authoredOn is pharmacy entertime (:55,124), not either endpoint, and no other served element preserves them; the direct and medication-mix branches were both covered. All 18 differing_conflict rows replay the TIMESTAMPTZ cast at :43-44 exactly with residual_rows 0, which is why the comparator tiered this gap_shaped rather than contested. The loss is ancillary, not essential: nsaid applies no temporal filter, has no carry-forward, and its grain (subject_id, hadm_id, drug) survives intact. Three concepts hit the identical ETL statement in the identical columns and were judge-accepted -- acei 91.91% identical with 9,059 null-only, arb 91.95% with 3,179, antibiotic 94.08% with 43,453. nsaid is 95.63% identical with 10,276 (4.4%): the highest fidelity and the lowest null fraction of the four, and the only one blocked. antibiotic's start times genuinely drive downstream suspicion-of-infection windows and were accepted with four times the missing rows, so the essential/ancillary line was not drawn where the ruling put it.
